headline: Inside every seed is a tiny plant waiting for its moment
universal_truth: Potential often hides in small, unassuming packages
fun_facts: A 2,000-year-old date palm seed found in Israel was successfully germinated in 2005
The world's smallest seeds belong to orchids—a million of them weigh less than a gram
A single sunflower head can contain up to 2,000 seeds, each capable of growing a new plant
discussion_questions: What 'seeds' of potential are you carrying that haven't sprouted yet?
What conditions do you need to grow?
How do you nurture the seeds in others?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Hold a seed in your hand. You're holding a tiny time capsule—a complete blueprint for a future plant, sometimes containing DNA unchanged for millions of years. Inside that small shell is everything needed to become a towering tree. Let's look inside.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Seeds can wait. Some for decades, others for centuries—even millennia. Scientists germinated a 2,000-year-old seed found in Israel. How can something stay alive for so long while appearing completely dead?
cliff.prompt: What keeps a seed alive for thousands of years?

options.text: The seed is essentially in suspended animation
options.response: Yes. Seeds enter dormancy, slowing their metabolism to almost zero until conditions are right.

options.text: The hard shell protects it from decay
options.response: The shell helps, but there's more to the story...

q1.title: The Methuselah Seed
q1.script: In 2005, scientists in Israel sprouted a date palm seed that had been buried for 2,000 years. They named it Methuselah. That seed waited through the rise and fall of empires, through plagues and wars—and then it grew. Patience encoded in DNA.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Methuselah Seed"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Dust-Sized Giants
q2.script: Orchid seeds are so small that a million weigh less than a gram. They're little more than embryos wrapped in thin coats. Yet each contains the complete instructions to build an orchid. The greatest things often come in the smallest packages.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Sunflower Abundance
q3.script: One sunflower head can hold 2,000 seeds. Each seed can grow a plant that produces 2,000 more seeds. Do the math: one sunflower's descendants could theoretically cover Earth in just a few generations. Nature thinks in abundance.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You are a seed that sprouted. Every skill you have, every insight—they were once tiny potentials waiting for the right conditions. And you're still growing. You're still becoming what you will be.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 6. Tomorrow, we'll look up at night and discover what stars are truly made of. Until then, consider: what seeds are you planting today?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Planting Seeds - Small Beginnings
growTrack.learning_objective: Start something new, no matter how small
growTrack.activity: Plant one small 'seed' today—start a 5-minute project, send a message to reconnect with someone, or write the first paragraph of something. Don't worry about the harvest; just plant.
